title: The 1936-37 personnel turnover in the Hines band
summary: Many sidemen quit or got notice; Ray Nance's men arrived.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Just, you know, looking at the recordings from 1929 to 1940 seems to be four distinct bands. The first band, and then the 1931 band, and then there was a big change in the middle of 1937.

Yeah, I was going to say '36, but I know -- that's when Hayes Alvis came into the band. We changed the brass section, they changed the -- little-George Dixon was still with us. Then we got Milton Fletcher on trumpet.
Right.
And we still had Billy Franklin on trombone until he got hurt. That was in 1936 when he got hurt. Then we got Kenneth Stuart on trombone in Billy Franklin's place.
Now, in the summer of '37, according to the recordings, you know, the recording personnel, there was only you and George Dixon and Louis Taylor from the previous band.
From the previous band.
Everybody else was new.
I imagine -- yeah, that's about right.
What caused that?
I don't know.
Well, I mean did Earl fire the other guys?
No. Some of them just quit, you know, went with other bands.
But it was an awful lot of them quit, all -- I guess all about the same time.
Well, often times -- almost the same, but one time he had almost like a wholesale firing.
Was that in '37?
I think he give -- yeah, I think he give about five notices. That's when what's his name -- Ray
Nance came with the band on trumpet and violin.
Right.
In fact, we got some of Ray Nance's men with us.
Yeah, Ray had the band at DeLisa, didn't he?
No, at the -- what was the name of that club? 61st and Michigan. Yeah, Ray Nance, Oliver Coleman, and I'm trying to think of the piano player's name. LeRoy Harris on saxophone.
He came with Earl?
He came with Earl. He came with Ray Nance, like with that Ray Nance band.
